stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 8%, and then the new price is decreased by 45%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 8% increase: $100 \times (1 + 8/100) = 108.00$. After a 45% decrease on 108.00: $108.00 \times (1 - 45/100) = 59.40$. Net change $= 59.40 - 100 = -40.60\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 8 - 45 - \dfrac{360}{100} = -40.60\%$.
